name: Messenger M1 — real unread badges for channels (human + AI messages)
description:
Implemented channel unread badges for the messenger by adding a shared `isUnreadForUser`/`countChannelUnread` rule in `client/src/utils/chatUnread.js`, leaving the kanban/wall rule untouched.

Added a derived `channelUnreadCounts` getter to the chats store, computed from loaded messages and `$storex.users.user.username`, with nothing persisted on the chat.

Updated `MessengerChannelList.vue` to take an `unreadCounts` prop and render the badge on both the collapsed avatar and the expanded row.

Wired `MessengerView.vue` to pass the counts, mark a channel as seen on open via the real `markMessageAsSeen({ chat_id, message_id, username })` action, and render `MessengerGroupInfo` on desktop and mobile.

Result: badges appear for messages from other users or assistant replies and clear instantly once `read_by` is patched, with no reload and no changes to `MessengerGroupInfo.vue`.

messages.content:
Objective: a channel shows a correct unread badge and clears it when opened — for BOTH human messages and AI profile replies. This is the signal the whole "read Slack from the phone while away" promise depends on.

Why this profile: `VueDeveloper` owns the Vue component structure + the Pinia/Vuex-style store code that has to change together.

Current defect (verified):
1. `MessengerChannelList.vue` renders `chat.unread_count` (expanded rows and collapsed avatars), but nothing in `client/src/store/chats.js` ever sets `unread_count` → badges never appear.
2. The real unread rule is `client/src/utils/chatUnread.js#isUnreadMessage`, which requires `message.role === 'assistant'` → human-to-human messages are NEVER unread, which breaks the team-chat use case.

Steps:
1. In `client/src/utils/chatUnread.js`, add `isUnreadForUser(message, username, { includeUserMessages })`: keep the existing assistant rule as the default (do not change kanban/wall behaviour) and allow counting `role === 'user'` messages authored by someone else when the caller asks for it (channels). Export a `countChannelUnread(messages, username)` helper.
2. In `client/src/store/chats.js`, add a getter `channelUnreadCount: (state) => (chatId) => number` (or a `channelsWithUnread` getter) that derives the count from the chat messages + current username via the new helper. Do NOT persist anything new on the chat.
3. In `MessengerChannelList.vue`, replace `chat.unread_count` with the derived value passed in as a prop (`:unread-count="..."`) computed by `MessengerView.vue` — the list component must stay dumb.
4. In `MessengerView.vue#openChat`, after loading the channel, mark the unseen messages as read with the existing `$storex.chats.markMessageAsSeen` for the current user (`this.$user?.username`), then let the badge clear reactively.
5. Keep the collapsed/expanded rendering and Tailwind-only styling as-is; no `<style>` additions beyond what exists.

Acceptance:
- Two sessions (two users, or one user + one profile reply) → the second user sees "1", "2"… on the channel row and on the collapsed avatar.
- Opening the channel clears the badge without a page reload.
- Kanban task cards and the activity wall keep their current unread behaviour (no regression).
- No console errors; `chat.unread_count` no longer referenced anywhere.

Target: D+5 (M1 demo).

Objective: implement M1 in `client/` — a channel shows a correct unread badge (human AND profile messages) that clears when opened, and the channel members panel is reachable on desktop and mobile. This is the increment that is demoed on Fri Nov 6; it must be deployable and demoable on its own.

Why these profiles: `VueDeveloper` owns the Vue component structure + Options-API store wiring; `file_editor` produces the complete file contents (no partial patches).

## Verified facts — use them, but confirm before editing
1. `client/src/utils/chatUnread.js` exports `isUnreadMessage(message, username)` and `countUnreadMessages(messages, username)`. Current rule: `role === 'assistant' && user !== username && !read_by.includes(username) && done !== false && !hide`.
2. `client/src/components/messenger/MessengerChannelList.vue` is Options API (props/emits/data/computed/methods inside `<script>`). It renders `chat.unread_count > 0` in TWO places: the collapsed avatar badge and the expanded row badge.
3. `client/src/components/messenger/MessengerGroupInfo.vue` ALREADY exists and is complete. Props: `chat`, `profiles`. Emits: `close`, `update-members`, `update-name`, `leave-group`. It is imported by `MessengerView.vue` but never rendered. Do NOT rewrite it — only render and wire it.
4. `client/src/views/MessengerView.vue` already has `showGroupInfo` (currently only toggles a button colour), `membersLabel`, `updateGroupMembers(profiles)`, `updateGroupName(name)`, `leaveGroup(chat)`, `profiles`, `loadProfiles()`, `openChat(chat)`.
5. IMPORTANT: before writing step 5, open `client/src/store/chats.js` and confirm the real "mark messages as read" action name. The plan says `markMessageAsSeen`; if the real name differs, use the real one and state it in your summary. Do NOT invent a new action, a new API endpoint or a new backend field.

## Steps
1. `chatUnread.js` — leave `isUnreadMessage` / `countUnreadMessages` EXACTLY as they are (kanban task cards and the activity wall must not regress). Add:
   - `isUnreadForUser(message, username, options = {})`: same rules as today, plus when `options.includeUserMessages` is true a `role === 'user'` message authored by someone else counts as unread.
   - `countChannelUnread(messages, username)`: `countChannelUnread` → counts with `includeUserMessages: true`.
2. `store/chats.js` — add a derived, reactive accessor (getter) that returns a map `{ [chatId]: count }` for channels (`mode === 'channel'`) computed from each chat's `messages` via `countChannelUnread` and the current username in the store. Do NOT persist `unread_count` on the chat and do NOT mutate the chat objects. Read `state.user` / the existing user source rather than inventing one.
3. `MessengerView.vue` — add a computed `unreadCounts` fed by that accessor; pass `:unread-counts="unreadCounts"` to BOTH `MessengerChannelList` instances (desktop sidebar and mobile drawer).
4. `MessengerChannelList.vue` — add prop `unreadCounts: { type: Object, default: () => ({}) }` and replace BOTH `chat.unread_count` expressions with `(unreadCounts[chat.id] || 0)`. Keep the component dumb (no store access, no computation).
5. `MessengerView.vue#openChat` — after `loadChat` resolves, mark the channel's messages as seen for `this.$user?.username` with the real store action found in step 5 of the facts above, so the badge clears reactively without a reload.
6. `MessengerView.vue` — render the members panel:
   - Desktop: right-side panel after the main area, `v-if="activeChat && showGroupInfo"`, `<MessengerGroupInfo :chat="activeChat" :profiles="profiles" @close="showGroupInfo = false" @update-members="updateGroupMembers" @update-name="updateGroupName" @leave-group="leaveGroup" />`.
   - Mobile: full-screen overlay `fixed inset-0 z-50` replacing the drawer/bottom nav, same bindings, `v-if="isMobile && activeChat && showGroupInfo"`.
   - The existing mobile bottom-nav "Members" button must then work with no change.
7. Cosmetic but required (it breaks the light theme): remove the inline `style="background: #111111;"` on the root div → use `bg-base-100`; and fix the invalid bare `hover:` classes (Tailwind class with no value) in `MessengerView.vue` and `MessengerChannelList.vue` by giving them real values.

## Code rules (mandatory)
- Imports only inside `<script setup>`; no variables, refs or logic there.
- `data()` / `computed` / `watch` / `methods` inside the exported object; access via `this.`.
- No semicolons. TailwindCSS only — no new `<style>` rules and no inline styles (the existing `<style scoped>` transition classes may stay).
- Methods under ~15 lines.

## Acceptance (report each one in your summary)
- `grep -r "unread_count" client/src` returns nothing.
- `isUnreadMessage` / `countUnreadMessages` behaviour unchanged (kanban + wall safe).
- `MessengerGroupInfo` rendered in both layouts with all 4 emits wired and `profiles` passed.
- Two sessions: a colleague's message lights "1" on the channel row and on the collapsed avatar; opening the channel clears it without reload; a profile reply also counts.
- List the files changed with a one-line description of each change.
If a step is impossible, stop and write the exact blocker instead of a partial implementation.
